newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi warns pilgrims over political material, acts.
newsitem.headline: Saudi warns pilgrims over political material, acts.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Thursday warned pilgrims they would face tough punishment if they carried political material at the annual Moslem pilgrimage due in April this year.
The Saudi Interior Ministry warned pilgrims in a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) against carrying any books, pictures or publications that have "a political or propaganda aim".
It said "anybody found to be in possession of anything forbidden, no matter what its kind is, will be severely punished...without any leniency or toleration".
The ministry, which issues similar warnings before haj every year, did not elaborate.
Up to two million Moslems perfom haj at Mecca and Medina, two of Islam's holiest shrines, every year.

Shi'ite clerics ruling Iran since the 1979 Islamic revolution say Moslems had a right to air their political grievances during the pilgrimage, mainly through rallies against Israel and the United States.
Saudi's conservative Sunni rulers say the haj, which draws Moslems from around the world, is a purely religious exercise.
Saudi security forces clashed in 1987 with demonstrators in an Iranian-led rally in the streets of Mecca, killing about 400 people, mainly Iranians.

Iran boycotted the haj for the next three years. There has been no repeat of the bloodshed since the return of Iranian pilgrims in 1991 and their haj rallies have been low-key affairs confined to the Iranian compounds.
